sections.purpose: To estimate haemoglobin concentration in blood using the acid haematin method with Sahli's haemoglobinometer as part of pharmacology and clinical pharmacy practicals.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for haemoglobin estimation experiments in clinical pharmacology practicals.
procedure: Fill the graduated tube of the haemoglobinometer with N/10 HCl up to the 2 g% mark (lower graduation).
Clean the fingertip of the subject with 70% alcohol and allow it to dry.
Prick the fingertip firmly with a sterile lancet to obtain a free-flowing drop of blood.
Wipe away the first drop of blood.
Draw blood into the Sahli pipette exactly up to the 20 cubic mm (0.02 mL) mark — avoid air bubbles.
Wipe the outside of the pipette immediately with a clean tissue.
Blow the blood from the pipette into the acid in the graduated tube immediately.
Rinse the pipette 2–3 times with the acid solution in the tube.
Mix gently by stirring with a glass rod.
Allow the tube to stand for 10 minutes to ensure complete conversion of haemoglobin to acid haematin.
Add distilled water drop by drop using a dropper, stirring after each addition, until the colour of the solution matches the standard brown glass colour of the comparator.
Read the haemoglobin value directly from the scale on the graduated tube (in g/dL or % value).
Record the reading and note normal reference ranges: Male 13–17 g/dL; Female 12–15 g/dL.
Clean all glassware with distilled water followed by 70% ethanol after use.
Dispose of lancets in sharps containers and blood-contaminated materials in biohazard waste.
precautions: Ensure the graduated tube is filled with N/10 HCl to the correct starting mark before adding blood.
Draw exactly 20 mm³ of blood — excess or deficit blood will give inaccurate results.
Allow exactly 10 minutes for complete acid haematin formation before colour matching.
Perform colour matching in diffuse natural daylight — avoid direct sunlight or artificial light.
Wear gloves when handling blood samples; follow universal blood/body fluid precautions.
Use sterile disposable lancets — never reuse lancets.
Dispose of all sharps in approved sharps containers immediately after use.
Note that Sahli's method has limited accuracy compared to photometric methods; results may vary ±10%.
